record.original_question: For the class of continuous critical measures that arises when Heine-Stieltjes zeros are modeled as critical configurations rather than global minimizers, can one find a feasible description of the resulting multi-parameter family of continuous critical measures?

evidence.quote: If we are analyzing Heine-Stieltjes polynomials whose zeros provide a critical configuration for the total energy E(X) (but not the global minimum!), then what measure mu should we expect in the semiclassical limit?

However, in this description two open problems remain: (i) to prove that discrete critical measures converge in the thermodynamic limit to continuous critical measures, and that all continuous critical measures can be obtained this way; (ii) to find a feasible description of the multi-parametric family of continuous critical measures in the given class.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. For a finite set of distinct points $A=\{a_0,a_1,\dots,a_p\}\subset\mathbb{C}$ (with prescribed positive masses $\alpha_0,\dots,\alpha_p>0$ for the "external field" / weights) and an integer $n\ge 1$, consider configurations $X=\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}$ of $n$ points in $\mathbb{C}\setminus A$. Define the total logarithmic energy
$$E(X)=\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}\log\frac{1}{|x_i-x_j|}+\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{k=0}^{p}\alpha_k\log\frac{1}{|x_i-a_k|}.$$
A configuration $X$ is called a discrete critical configuration if $\nabla E(X)=0$; equivalently, $X$ is the zero set of a Heine–Stieltjes polynomial associated with $A$ and the weights $\alpha_k$. The normalized counting measure of $X$ is the corresponding discrete critical measure.

A finite positive Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{C}$ with compact support is called a continuous critical measure (for the data $(A,\alpha_0,\dots,\alpha_p)$) if it is a saddle point of the weighted logarithmic energy functional in the appropriate sense — concretely, if there exists a rational function $R$ with poles only in $A$ such that, with $C^{\mu}(z)=\int\frac{d\mu(t)}{z-t}$ the Cauchy transform of $\mu$, one has $(C^{\mu}(z)-\sum_k \alpha_k/(z-a_k))^2 = R(z)$ for $z\in\mathbb{C}\setminus(\mathrm{supp}\,\mu\cup A)$ (so the support of $\mu$ lies on critical trajectories of a quadratic differential $-R(z)\,dz^2$).

Problem. Give a feasible (explicit and effectively parameterized) description of the entire multi-parameter family of continuous critical measures in this class. That is, identify the natural parameters (e.g. the free coefficients of the rational function $R$, the homology/combinatorial data of the critical graph of the quadratic differential, periods of $\sqrt{R}\,dz$, etc.) and characterize, in terms of these parameters, which choices arise as continuous critical measures, together with a constructive procedure to recover $\mu$ from the parameters.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Martínez-Finkelshtein, Rakhmanov and collaborators (notably the 2009/2011 paper on critical measures, quadratic differentials and weak limits of zeros of Stieltjes polynomials, and follow-ups on higher Heine–Stieltjes polynomials and on critical measures on higher-genus Riemann surfaces, e.g. arXiv:2207.02068) has further developed the link between continuous critical measures and quadratic differentials, but no explicit and fully effective parameterization of the entire multi-parameter family of continuous critical measures in this class appears to have been established. The problem is generally still regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Critical measures, quadratic differentials, and weak limits of zeros of Stieltjes polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Continuous critical measures characterized as saddle points of weighted logarithmic energy, related to quadratic differentials with closed trajectories.
status_evidence.claim: Develops the framework but does not provide a complete feasible parameterization of all such measures.

status_evidence.title: On higher Heine-Stieltjes polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Studies generalizations and multiparameter spectral problems for Heine–Stieltjes-type polynomial solutions.
status_evidence.claim: Extends the theory but the description of the multi-parametric family of continuous critical measures remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Critical measures on higher genus Riemann surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent extension of the theory of critical measures to higher genus settings.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the subject is still actively developed, with no definitive feasible parameterization in the original class.
